arxiv-2001-07397.creator: Chong Shen, Xiaoyong Xi, Xiaoquan Xu, Dongsheng Zhao
arxiv-2001-07397.description: Abstract . We introduce and study a new class of T 0 T_{0} spaces, called open well-filtered spaces. The main results we prove include (i) every well-filtered space is an open well-filtered space; (ii) every core-compact open well-filtered space is sober. As an immediate corollary, it follows that every core-compact well-filtered space is sober.

arxiv-2104-14241.title: Integral Line-of-Sight Path Following Control of Magnetic Helical Microswimmers Subject to Step-Out Frequencies
arxiv-2104-14241.creator: Alireza Mohammadi, Mark W. Spong
arxiv-2104-14241.description: Abstract This paper investigates the problem of straight-line path following for magnetic helical microswimmers. The control objective is to make the helical microswimmer to converge to a straight line without violating the step-out frequency constraint. arxiv-2107-13760.title: Viewpoint-Invariant Exercise Repetition Counting
arxiv-2107-13760.creator: Yu Cheng Hsu, Qingpeng Zhang, Efstratios Tsougenis, Kwok-Leung Tsui
arxiv-2107-13760.description: Abstract Counting the repetition of human exercise and physical rehabilitation is a common task in rehabilitation and exercise training. The existing vision-based repetition counting methods less emphasize the concurrent motions in the same video. This work presents a vision-based human motion repetition counting applicable to counting concurrent motions through the skeleton location extracted from various pose estimation methods.

arxiv-2207-10281.title: Multi-element flow-driven spectral chaos (ME-FSC) method for uncertainty quantification of dynamical systems Journal: Journal of Computational Physics (Elsevier)
arxiv-2207-10281.creator: Hugo Esquivel, Arun Prakash, Guang Lin
arxiv-2207-10281.description: Abstract The flow-driven spectral chaos (FSC) is a recently developed method for tracking and quantifying uncertainties in the long-time response of stochastic dynamical systems using the spectral approach. The method uses a novel concept called enriched stochastic flow maps as a means to construct an evolving finite-dimensional random function space that is both accurate and computationally efficient in time.

arxiv-2301-06199.title: Doubly Robust Counterfactual Classification
arxiv-2301-06199.creator: Kwangho Kim, Edward H. Kennedy, José R. Zubizarreta
arxiv-2301-06199.description: Abstract We study counterfactual classification as a new tool for decision-making under hypothetical (contrary to fact) scenarios. We propose a doubly-robust nonparametric estimator for a general counterfactual classifier, where we can incorporate flexible constraints by casting the classification problem as a nonlinear mathematical program involving counterfactuals.

arxiv-2302-07740.title: Team Triple-Check at Factify 2: Parameter-Efficient Large Foundation Models with Feature Representations for Multi-Modal Fact Verification
arxiv-2302-07740.creator: Wei-Wei Du, Hong-Wei Wu, Wei-Yao Wang, Wen-Chih Peng
arxiv-2302-07740.description: Abstract Multi-modal fact verification has become an important but challenging issue on social media due to the mismatch between the text and images in the misinformation of news content, which has been addressed by considering cross-modalities to identify the veracity of the news in recent years.

arxiv-2410-17358.title: FairLoRA: Unpacking Bias Mitigation in Vision Models with Fairness-Driven Low-Rank Adaptation
arxiv-2410-17358.creator: Rohan SukumaranDIRO - Université de MontréalMila - Quebec AI Institute Québec, Canada rohan.sukumaran@umontreal.ca, Aarash FeiziMcGill UniversityMila - Quebec AI Institute Québec, Canada aarash.feizi@mcgill.ca Adriana Romero-SorianMcGill UniversityMila - Quebec AI Institute Québec, CanadaGolnoosh Fa
arxiv-2410-17358.description: Abstract Recent advances in parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods, such as Low Rank Adaptation (LoRA), have gained significant attention for their ability to efficiently adapt large foundational models to various downstream tasks. These methods are appreciated for achieving performance comparable to full fine-tuning on aggregate-level metrics, while significantly reducing computational costs.

arxiv-2503-16068.title: PoseTraj : Pose-Aware Trajectory Control in Video Diffusion
arxiv-2503-16068.creator: Longbin Ji, Lei Zhong, Pengfei Wei, Changjian Li
arxiv-2503-16068.description: Abstract Recent advancements in trajectory-guided video generation have achieved notable progress. However, existing models still face challenges in generating object motions with potentially changing 6D poses under wide-range rotations, due to limited 3D understanding. To address this problem, we introduce PoseTraj , a pose-aware video dragging model for generating 3D-aligned motion from 2D trajectories.

arxiv-2504-06512.title: ICPS: Real-Time Resource Configuration for Cloud Serverless Functions Considering Affinity
arxiv-2504-06512.creator: Long Chen, Xinshuai Hua, Jinquan Zhang, Wenshuai Li, Xiaoping Li, Shijie Guo
arxiv-2504-06512.description: Abstract Serverless computing, with its operational simplicity and on-demand scalability, has become a preferred paradigm for deploying workflow applications. However, resource allocation for workflows, particularly those with branching structures, is complicated by cold starts and network delays between dependent functions, significantly degrading execution efficiency and response times.

arxiv-2505-15647.title: Second-Order Convergence in Private Stochastic Non-Convex Optimization
arxiv-2505-15647.creator: Youming Tao, Zuyuan Zhang, Dongxiao Yu, Xiuzhen Cheng, Falko Dressler, Di Wang
arxiv-2505-15647.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Youming Tao, Zuyuan Zhang, Dongxiao Yu, Xiuzhen Cheng, Falko Dressler, Di Wang. We investigate the problem of finding second-order stationary points (SOSP) in differentially private (DP) stochastic non-convex optimization. Existing methods suffer from two key limitations: (i) inaccurate convergence error rate due to overlooking gradient variance in the saddle point escape analysis, and (ii) dependence on auxiliary private model selection procedures for identifying DP-SOSP, which can significantly impair utility, particularly in distributed settings.

arxiv-2509-11755.title: Time to Play: Simulating Early-Life Animal Dynamics Enhances Robotics Locomotion Discovery
arxiv-2509-11755.creator: Paul Templier, Hannah Janmohamed, David Labonte, Antoine Cully
arxiv-2509-11755.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Paul Templier, Hannah Janmohamed, David Labonte, Antoine Cully. Developmental changes in body morphology profoundly shape locomotion in animals, yet artificial agents and robots are typically trained under static physical parameters. Inspired by ontogenetic scaling of muscle power in biology, we propose Scaling Mechanical Output over Lifetime (SMOL) , a novel curriculum that dynamically modulates robot actuator strength to mimic natural variations in power-to-weight ratio during growth and ageing.

pmc-11594174.creator: Sabrina Pagano, Emmanuel Somm, Catherine Juillard, Nicolas Liaudet, Frédérique Ino, Johan Ferrari, Vincent Braunersreuther, François R Jornayvaz, Nicolas Vuilleumier, Rosaria Maria Pipitone, Stefania Grimaudo
pmc-11594174.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MASLD) is a common liver and health issue associated with heightened cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk, with Cytokeratin 18 (CK-18) as a marker of liver injury across the MASLD to cirrhosis spectrum. Autoantibodies against apolipoprotein A-1 (AAA-1s) predict increased CVD risk, promoting atherosclerosis and liver steatosis in apoE−/− mice, though their impact on liver inflammation and fibrosis remains unclear.

pmc-12404456.title: Willingness to use long-acting injectable pre-exposure prophylaxis (LAI-PrEP) among black cisgender women in the Southern United States
pmc-12404456.creator: Sylvia Shangani, Jaquetta M. Reeves, Kristin Heron, Jessica M. Sales, Kenneth K. Mugwanya
pmc-12404456.description: BackgroundLong-acting injectable pre-exposure prophylaxis (LAI-PrEP) for HIV prevention may improve adherence for those with concerns with daily pills. Limited data exist on LAI-PrEP acceptability among Black women in the U.S., a population vulnerable to HIV. We assessed willingness to use LAI-PrEP among Black women eligible for PrEP in the Southern U.S.

pmc-13028275.title: Hybrid Vision Transformer–CNN Framework for Alzheimer’s Disease Cell Type Classification: A Comparative Study with Vision–Language Models
pmc-13028275.creator: Md Easin Hasan, Md Tahmid Hasan Fuad, Omar Sharif, Amy Wagler
pmc-13028275.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Accurate identification of Alzheimer’s disease (AD)-related cellular characteristics from microscopy images is essential for understanding neurodegenerative mechanisms at the cellular level. While most computational approaches focus on macroscopic neuroimaging modalities, cell type classification from microscopy remains relatively underexplored. In this study, we propose a hybrid vision transformer–convolutional neural network (ViT–CNN) framework that integrates DeiT-Small and EfficientNet-B7 to classify three AD-related cell types—astrocytes, cortical neurons, and SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells—from phase-contrast microscopy images.

pmc-13101295.title: Two-dimensional SnSe2/Bi2Se3 vertically stacked heterostructures for enhanced photoresponse through tuning layer coverage
pmc-13101295.creator: Liying Wen, Dongsheng Hu, Ruihong Zhang, Xiaoxiang Hu, Yan Luo, Hui Chen, Yifang Liang, Yong Li, Shifeng Wang
pmc-13101295.description: SummaryTwo-dimensional (2D) materials have attracted much attention due to their unique structures and excellent optoelectronic properties. In this work, we fabricated c-axis-aligned SnSe2/Bi2Se3 2D heterostructures via a hydrothermal technique, where the epitaxial growth of Bi2Se3 nanoplates is achieved on SnSe2 microplate substrates. The electronic states at the interfaces can be regulated facilely via tuning the Bi2Se3 nanoplate coverage.

pmc-13376765.description: Interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome (IC/BPS) is a chronic inflammatory condition with limited treatments. This study identifies CCR1’s role in IC/BPS and evaluates CCR1 inhibition as a therapeutic strategy.
